html:
SMTO-SKL-0045 — The Drive upload was interrupted and can't be continued

GUID: 3c9cf011-c417-5841-8498-4d0d03a524b3
Slug: google-drive-upload-session-expired
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Google ended the upload before SMTO finished sending the file, so it can't pick up where it left off. The file most likely wasn't finished in Drive, but check before uploading again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: open the destination folder in Google Drive and look for the file by name and size, or check a replaced file's size and date. If Google did keep a complete copy, uploading again would create a duplicate.
  2. If you find the file and it opens correctly, keep it and don't upload again. That copy is already complete, so another upload would only add a duplicate.
  3. If the file isn't there, ask SMTO to upload it again and approve the request. A new upload starts a fresh session with Google.

What success looks like

  • Exactly one copy of the file is in the Drive folder, at the expected size.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep starting new uploads without checking Drive between attempts.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned HTTP 404 or 410 for the resumable upload session URL, so the session can no longer accept data.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 404 or 410 for the resumable upload session. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 404 or 410 for the resumable upload session.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact correlation and Drive file state before creating another session.

How to fix it

  • provider_error mapped a 404/410 on the resumable session to upload_session_expired. Before starting a new upload, confirm no completed upload exists: for upload, search for a file whose smto_operation appProperty matches the operation; for replace_contents, compare the target file's size, md5Checksum and modifiedTime. Then start one deliberate new upload rather than repeating blindly.
  • Inspect the exact correlation and Drive state before starting a new upload; do not blindly repeat.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact correlation and Drive state before starting a new upload; do not blindly repeat.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing upload effects are reconciled before a deliberate replacement session.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
